findings_to_judge.finding: July 2026 was the warmest month in the entire 131-year contiguous-US temperature record (76.9degF, all 48 states above their 20th-century average, none near or below normal) and it is the final and seasonally largest month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, which ended 31 July 2026 - record cooling load is the direct driver of the emergency HVAC service calls and same-day replacement tickets that flow through Gross Transaction Volume and the payments take-rate, i.e. the ~25% of revenue that is variable ($66.8m of the $268.8m reported in Q1 was non-subscription).

ServiceTitan bills roughly $245-400 per technician per month, so its subscription line is mechanically a function of how many technicians its contractors employ - and BLS JOLTS shows construction hires in July 2026, the last month of ServiceTitan's fiscal Q2, at 366,000, up 14.7% month-over-month and 9.9% year-over-year, the highest construction hiring rate in about two years, with openings at 326,000 (+9.4% m/m).

The visible HVAC datapoint an analyst would cross-read into ServiceTitan is Lennox's 30-July print - residential revenue -7%, unit volume -12%, full-year growth guide cut from ~4% to ~1% - but that is a company-specific channel and share story (Lennox's own one-step volumes fell mid-teens, new construction -30%), while the industry-wide series over the same window went the other way: Watsco, the largest US HVAC distributor, reported domestic residential HVAC equipment sales +5% with unit volume +2% and ASPs +2% and titled its release 'further industry stabilization'; Lennox's own CEO said the repair-versus-replace trend 'has stabilized', and a repair-skewed market with record heat maximises job count and technician demand, which is what ServiceTitan monetises rather than equipment units.
